paragraphs.title: A Plea for Compassion, Protection, and Salvation

easy.explanation: He says, “I am poor and needy.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe his condition?
What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do for his soul?

easy.explanation: He says, “I cry unto thee daily.”
easy.q: When does the psalmist cry unto the LORD?

answers: Because he is poor and needy
Because he is king of the nations
Because his enemies have already surrendered
medium.explanation: His poverty and need are given as the reason for his plea.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD to hear him?

medium.explanation: He asks, “Rejoice the soul of thy servant.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do to his soul?

medium.explanation: Supplications are earnest requests or pleas.

answers: He asks for salvation because he trusts in God
He says that he does not know God
He wants to hide his faith
challenge.explanation: He calls himself God's servant who trusts in Him and asks to be saved.
challenge.q: What connection does the psalmist make between his faithfulness and his request for salvation?

answers: That the psalmist needs no help
That he urgently needs God to hear and respond
That he is speaking to his enemies
challenge.explanation: He repeatedly asks God to give ear, attend, and answer him.
challenge.q: What does the repeated request for God to hear and answer emphasize?

answers: The LORD is good, ready to forgive, and plenteous in mercy
The LORD always hides His face
The LORD does not hear prayer
challenge.explanation: The psalmist relies on God's goodness, forgiveness, and abundant mercy.
challenge.q: Which description of the LORD strengthens the psalmist's hope?

answers: There is none like Him among the gods
He is one of many equal gods
He is like every human being
easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Among the gods there is none like unto thee.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe God's uniqueness?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “All nations whom thou hast made shall come.”
easy.q: Who will come and worship before the LORD?

easy.explanation: They will worship before Him and glorify His name.
easy.q: What will the nations do before the LORD?

answers: Because they do not know Him
medium.explanation: The verse identifies them as nations whom God has made.
medium.q: Why will all nations come before the LORD?

answers: God's unique greatness is shown by His works
His wonders cancel out His uniqueness
medium.explanation: God's wondrous works demonstrate that He is unlike any other.
medium.q: What is the relationship between “there is none like unto thee” and “doest wondrous things”?

medium.explanation: Wondrous things are extraordinary works that inspire wonder.
medium.q: What does “wondrous things” mean in this passage?

answers: The psalmist moves from personal prayer to universal recognition of God's greatness
He moves from praising God to denying Him
He moves from describing nations to discussing his wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage expands from the psalmist's prayer to the worship of God by all nations.
challenge.q: What change in thought takes place in these verses?

answers: Recognition of God's greatness and uniqueness
challenge.explanation: The nations honor God because they recognize His greatness.
challenge.q: What does worshiping and glorifying God's name signify here?

answers: God alone is great in His being and works
The nations are stronger than God
The psalmist is asking for wealth
challenge.explanation: These verses emphasize God's uniqueness, greatness, and wondrous works.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by verses 8–10?

paragraphs.title: Guidance, an Undivided Heart, and Thanksgiving

easy.explanation: He prays, “Teach me thy way, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to teach him?

easy.explanation: He asks God to unite his heart “to fear thy name.”
easy.q: Why does the psalmist ask God to unite his heart?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee... with all my heart.”
easy.q: How will the psalmist praise the LORD?

answers: Learning God's way leads to living according to His truth
Learning God's way leads away from truth
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks to be taught God's way so that he may walk in His truth.
medium.q: What is the connection between learning God's way and walking in His truth?

answers: Because of God's great mercy and deliverance
Because his enemies commanded him to do so
Because he wants to forget his past
medium.explanation: He remembers God's great mercy and the deliverance of his soul.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist promise to glorify God's name forevermore?

answers: Make his heart devoted and undivided in fearing God
Divide his heart among many purposes
medium.explanation: The expression describes a heart focused wholly on revering God.
medium.q: What does “unite my heart” mean in this context?

answers: The psalmist moves from asking for guidance to declaring praise for God's mercy and deliverance
He moves from praise to asking for enemies
He moves from describing nations to asking for wealth
challenge.explanation: He first asks for God's way and an undivided heart, then gives thanks for God's mercy.

answers: It is intended only for his enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes sincere, wholehearted praise.
challenge.q: What does “with all my heart” reveal about the psalmist's praise?

answers: They provide the reason for his continuing praise
They cause him to turn away from God
They prove that God did not answer him
challenge.explanation: God's mercy and deliverance are the foundation of his lasting commitment to glorify Him.
challenge.q: How are mercy and deliverance connected to the psalmist's promise to glorify God forever?

easy.explanation: The verse speaks of the proud and assemblies of violent men.
easy.q: Who has risen against the psalmist?
What have the violent men sought?

easy.explanation: The LORD is described as full of compassion and gracious.

answers: They have not set God before them
They do not know the psalmist
They do not want the psalmist's soul
medium.explanation: They act without placing God before them.
medium.q: What is wrong with the enemies according to the passage?

answers: The wicked seek the psalmist's life, while the LORD is compassionate
The poor are contrasted with the rich
The nations are contrasted with Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The psalmist contrasts violent enemies with God's compassionate character.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in verses 14–15?

medium.explanation: Longsuffering describes patience and a refusal to become quickly angry.

answers: It presents God as the source of compassion, mercy, and truth
It shows that God ignores him
It proves that the enemies are right
challenge.explanation: The psalmist rests his hope on God's compassionate and faithful character.
challenge.q: How does the description of God's character strengthen the psalmist against his enemies?

answers: He acts with kindness and faithfulness
He has no concern for people
challenge.explanation: The phrase joins God's loving mercy with His dependable truth.
challenge.q: What does the combination of “mercy and truth” suggest about God?

answers: It shows that they disregard God's will
It proves that they fear God
It shows that they have asked God for help
challenge.explanation: Their violence is portrayed as deliberate disregard for God.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the enemies have not set God before them?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Strength, Salvation, and a Sign of Goodness

easy.explanation: He asks, “Give thy strength unto thy servant.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to give His servant?

easy.explanation: He asks God to “save the son of thine handmaid.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do for the son of His handmaid?

easy.explanation: He asks that those who hate him may see it.
easy.q: Who will see the token for good?

answers: Turn to him, show mercy, give strength, and save him
Hide him from his enemies only
medium.explanation: The request includes God's turning toward him, mercy, strength, and salvation.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do before giving him a token for good?

answers: They will rejoice and become stronger
medium.explanation: The verse says that they will see it and be ashamed.
medium.q: What will happen to those who hate the psalmist when they see the token?

answers: A sign or evidence of God's favor
medium.explanation: The token is a visible sign that God is acting for the psalmist's good.

answers: It shows others that God has helped and comforted the psalmist
It proves that the enemies have won
challenge.explanation: The sign makes God's help and comfort evident to others.
challenge.q: What purpose does the token for good serve at the end of the psalm?

answers: Strength and salvation become visible evidence of God's favor
The ending cancels the request for mercy
The ending introduces an unrelated subject
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks not only for help but also for a visible sign of that help.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the earlier requests?

answers: Both describe God's beneficial care for the psalmist
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends by acknowledging God's past help and comfort.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “thou hast helped me” and “comforted me”?
